rows.subject: Societe Generale
rows.answer: Societe Generale has faced several investigations and fines in the past. In 2018, the bank was fined $1.3 billion for violating US sanctions against Sudan. In 2026, the bank was fined €20 million (~$23.3 million) by France’s insurance and banking regulator ACPR for failing to inform retail customers that its “Sobrio” bank account bundled an insurance policy, breaching pre-contractual transparency rules. In June 2025, French authorities searched Societe Generale's offices in Paris and in Luxembourg as part of a tax fraud investigation. The bank has declined to comment on the raids. In 2026, the bank was also fined $23 million for failing to disclose information to retail customers. The probe was triggered by the blocking by other US financial institutions in 2012 of two transactions that Societe Generale processed on behalf of a Sudanese sanctioned entity, according to the Justice Department.

rows.answer: UniCredit S.p.A. has been involved in a number of investigations and fines related to sanctions violations. It is important to note that these investigations and fines are not indicative of the bank's overall operations or financial stability, but rather specific instances of non-compliance with regulations.
